clue.text: That lady's family in extremely grievous pickles

indicators.note: in places the family words inside the ends of grievous
extremely means only the outermost letters of the next word are used

parts.note: first and last letters of grievous
that lady's is HER, her possessive
kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A woman's relatives find themselves in dreadful trouble, pickles in the sense of predicaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickles' reads as plural trouble, but it is the definition in its food sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Gherkins are small cucumbers preserved in vinegar, a common example of pickles.

clue.text: Grandpa, oddly fit, is a pleasure-seeker

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of Grandpa

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of Grandpa
a bout is a fit, as in a bout of coughing

explanation.surface: An elderly man who seems odd, though fit, lives for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is someone who goes from one social event or amusement to another.

clue.text: Message of half-hearted Austen work I put on line

indicators.note: put on places I in front of line in this down clue
half-hearted removes half of the double letter at the heart of the word

parts.note: Emma is a Jane Austen novel

explanation.surface: A note about an unenthusiastic attempt at a Jane Austen novel, sent down the line.
explanation.walkthrough: EMMA has MM at its heart; 'half-hearted' drops one of them, giving EMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent over the internet.

clue.text: Footballers who save energy run into stores

indicators.note: into places energy and run inside stores

parts.note: keeps means stores
E is the physics symbol for energy
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Goalkeepers who conserve their energy charge into the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like conserving energy, but belongs to the definition: goalkeepers make saves.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalkeepers, often just called keepers, are the players whose job is stopping shots.

clue.text: Some broken IT, school head's problem

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The school's computers are broken, and the headteacher has to deal with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the head teacher, but the problem is on a scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: Nits are the eggs of head lice, a common problem for schoolchildren's scalps.

clue.text: The setter, after work, swallowed painkiller

indicators.note: after tells us the setter's letters come behind the work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
the setter refers to himself, so I
swallowed means ate

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler, back from the office, took a pill for a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'the setter', which gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, used to dull pain.

clue.text: Saucy R&B covers you heard creating trouble

indicators.note: covers means saucy and R&B together go around the sounded letter, which lands between them

parts.note: pert means saucy, cheeky
R&B, rhythm and blues, gives the letters R and B

indicators.note: heard means the word you is replaced by the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you

explanation.surface: Cheeky rhythm-and-blues cover versions that you listen to cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' works on both the saucy word and R&B together, so the sounded letter lands between them. 'creating' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb is to disturb or make anxious, a synonym of trouble as a verb.

clue.text: Model made by Jaguar with dome on top

indicators.note: on top puts the dome's letters above the car in this down clue

parts.note: a dome is a rounded arch-like vault, so arch
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A car model made by Jaguar with a domed roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a car model, but it means a prototype.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is an original pattern or typical example, a synonym of model.

clue.text: Slips water rat among cages

indicators.note: cages says the letters are held inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A water rat slips about between animal cages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is part of the hiding text, not the indicator; 'cages' holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors in printing or writing, i.e. slips.

clue.text: Geordie or Cockney, say, in charge of some philosophy

parts.note: Geordie (Tyneside) and Cockney (East London) are examples of a regional dialect

explanation.surface: A northerner or Londoner is put in charge of a branch of philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordie is the speech of Newcastle in north-east England; Cockney is the working-class speech of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is a method of philosophical argument that reasons through opposing ideas, as in Hegel or Socrates.

clue.text: German car parts arrive for business

indicators.note: parts means the word arrive splits to let the car in

parts.note: come means arrive
Merc is short for Mercedes, a German car

explanation.surface: Spare parts for a German car arrive for a trading firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the activity of buying and selling, i.e. business.

clue.text: Whizz in Rolls-Royce for fast driver

indicators.note: in places the expert inside the car's initials

parts.note: a whizz is an expert, an ace

explanation.surface: A speed demon behind the wheel of a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone who competes in speed contests, such as a racing driver.

clue.text: One's fired speculator before case of embezzlement

indicators.note: before puts the speculator ahead of the following letters

parts.note: a bull is a stock-market speculator who buys expecting prices to rise

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters of the word, its casing

parts.note: first and last letters of embezzlement

explanation.surface: Someone is sacked: a trader caught before an embezzlement case comes to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's fired' looks like dismissal from a job, but it is a gun's projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet is the projectile shot from a gun, so it is something fired.

clue.text: Fresh dessert European covered in chopped mint

indicators.note: covered in places the dessert and E inside the rearranged mint
chopped suggests the mint is cut up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: a new dessert from Europe, coated in chopped mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like a food word but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the informal sense of cheeky or forward is a synonym of impudent.

clue.text: Lloyd-Webber musical touring clubs everybody boos

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the musical encloses the other letters

parts.note: Cats is a musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A touring production of a Lloyd Webber musical is jeered at every venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Catcalls are shrill whistles or shouts of disapproval, like boos.

clue.text: Blimey! Sunak at dances in very distinctive fashion

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters jigging about into a new order

parts.note: Rishi Sunak, the former UK Prime Minister, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at the sight of Rishi Sunak dancing in a style all his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak is a former British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmistakeably means in a manner that cannot be confused with anything else, so very distinctively.

clue.text: What Buddhists do, lacking time for conflict resolution

indicators.note: lacking means losing one letter from the word

parts.note: Buddhists practise meditation

explanation.surface: Buddhist practice, done without rushing, helps settle disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is the intervention of a neutral party to settle a dispute.

clue.text: Cattle overturned lid for soup pan

parts.note: stock means farm animals, cattle

indicators.note: overturned means the word for a lid is read backwards

parts.note: a top is a lid

explanation.surface: Cows knock the lid off a pan of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a large deep pan for making stock and soups.

clue.text: Order bit of cash, hosting upper-class Republicans in DC

parts.note: to direct is to order

indicators.note: hosting means the coin holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a bit of cash
R is short for Republican, so RR for two of them

explanation.surface: An instruction to send money, with posh Republicans holding a fundraiser in Washington DC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DC' looks like Washington, the District of Columbia, but it is the electrical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: DC is the standard abbreviation for direct current, electricity flowing one way only.

clue.text: Rip neat pants? Put another coat on

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Torn smart trousers? Cover them with a new layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is the British slang for rubbish or poor, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaint is to apply a fresh coat of paint.

clue.text: Queen's following king loudly drinking a couple of rounds — they're on the house

indicators.note: following puts the queen's letters after the rest
drinking means the king and loudly take in the rounds

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
F is forte, the musical direction for loudly
two Os, round letters
ER is the Queen, and the 's gives ERS

explanation.surface: A noisy king, after the queen, buys a couple of rounds that are free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the house' looks like free drinks, but roofers work on a house's roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofers are tradespeople who lay and repair roofs, so their work is literally on top of a building.

clue.text: American, with help, eats starters of fowl roasted like a chicken

indicators.note: eats means the letters take in the first letters

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: starters of means the first letters of the following words

parts.note: first letter of fowl
first letter of roasted

explanation.surface: An American with a helper tucks into roast chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a chicken' looks culinary but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for cowardly, and someone afraid is scared like a coward.

clue.text: Staff in good Post Office entertained by funny fella

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside the rearranged fella
funny means odd, so the word fella is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Post Office workers are amused by a comical man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a pole, in particular one from which a flag is flown.

clue.text: Try mostly heavy, ornate kind of font

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: thick means heavy, dense

explanation.surface: Having a go with a bold, elaborate typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is a typeface style, also called blackletter, with heavy ornate strokes.

clue.text: Lacking in interest, laugh and sing softly

parts.note: ho is a laugh, as in ho ho
to hum is to sing softly with closed lips

explanation.surface: Someone bored laughs and hums a tune to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum is an expression of boredom, describing something dull.

clue.text: They might perform a duet or piano melody

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune, a melody

explanation.surface: Two singers might perform a duet, or a melody on the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two people, and a duet is performed by two.

clue.text: Defence from gangster, one getting bail occasionally

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of bail

parts.note: alternate letters of bail

explanation.surface: A mobster pleads his case while one of his gang is out on bail.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as a defence in court.

clue.text: Mushy peas, chips and rocket

indicators.note: mushy means mashed, so the letters are squashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A British chip-shop order: mushy peas, chips and rocket salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are mashed marrowfat peas served with fish and chips; 'rocket' looks like the salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a vehicle propelled into space, a kind of spaceship.

clue.text: Indicate peculiar need to grasp part of the Bible

indicators.note: to grasp means the rearranged need holds the following letters
peculiar means strange, so the word need is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Pointing out an odd urge to understand a passage of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or point to, a synonym of indicate.

clue.text: It lessens the shock of landing reckless mother in court

definitions.text: It lessens the shock of landing

indicators.note: in places the reckless mother inside court

parts.note: rash means reckless
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A rash mother is in court, the shock of the verdict softened.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash mat is a thick padded mat used in gymnastics to cushion falls.
